concepts.name: Article 5: Citizenship by Domicile at Commencement
key_dimensions: Three conditions: domicile in India, born in India, and parent born in India
Distinction between 'born in India' vs 'ordinarily resident in India'
Application to persons who migrated from Pakistan before July 19, 1948
UPSC trap: Article 5 vs Article 6 applicability based on migration date

concepts.name: Article 6: Rights of Citizenship of Migrants from Pakistan
key_dimensions: Two categories: migrants before July 19, 1948 (automatic) vs after (registration required)
Six months ordinary residence requirement for post-July 19, 1948 migrants
Distinction between 'registration' and 'naturalization' processes
UPSC trap: Cut-off date of July 19, 1948 vs March 1, 1947 in Article 7

concepts.name: Article 7: Rights of Migrants to Pakistan
key_dimensions: Disqualification of persons who migrated to Pakistan after March 1, 1947
Exception: Return to India under permit for resettlement or permanent return
Distinction between temporary visit and permanent return
UPSC trap: Different cut-off dates in Articles 6 and 7 (July 19, 1948 vs March 1, 1947)

concepts.name: Article 8: Rights of Overseas Citizens of Indian Origin
key_dimensions: Persons of Indian origin residing outside India
Registration as citizen if parent or grandparent born in undivided India
Countries where citizens are excluded from this provision (Pakistan, Bangladesh)
UPSC trap: Article 8 applies to persons outside India, not migrants within India

concepts.name: Article 9: Prohibition of Dual Citizenship
key_dimensions: Voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship terminates Indian citizenship
Automatic cessation without any formal procedure
Distinction between dual citizenship and Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) status
UPSC trap: OCI is not citizenship but a quasi-citizenship status

concepts.name: Article 10: Continuance of Citizenship Rights
key_dimensions: Subject to provisions of Part II, citizenship continues
Citizenship can be regulated by Parliament through law
Link to Citizenship Act, 1955 as implementing legislation
Constitutional vs statutory provisions on citizenship

concepts.name: Article 11: Parliament's Power to Regulate Citizenship
key_dimensions: Exclusive power of Parliament to make laws on citizenship
Covers acquisition, termination, and all other matters relating to citizenship
Not subject to Article 13 (laws inconsistent with fundamental rights)
UPSC trap: Article 11 laws are not subject to judicial review for violation of Part III

concepts.name: Domicile Requirement: Definition and Significance
key_dimensions: Domicile as permanent home vs ordinary residence as temporary stay
Domicile of origin, domicile of choice, and domicile by operation of law
Relevance in Articles 5 and 6 for citizenship determination
UPSC trap: Domicile in territory of India vs domicile in a particular state

concepts.name: Cut-off Dates: July 19, 1948 and March 1, 1947
key_dimensions: July 19, 1948: Date of registration of migrants from Pakistan (Article 6)
March 1, 1947: Cut-off for migration to Pakistan (Article 7)
Rationale behind different dates for different categories
UPSC trap: Confusion between these two critical dates in prelims questions

concepts.name: Partition and Citizenship: Constitutional Provisions
key_dimensions: Special provisions for partition-related migrations (Articles 6 and 7)
Asymmetry in treatment of migrants from vs to Pakistan
Historical context of communal violence and mass migrations
Temporary vs permanent migration distinction

concepts.name: Registration vs Naturalization: Distinction
key_dimensions: Registration: Simpler process for specific categories (Article 6, Article 8)
Naturalization: More stringent process for foreign nationals
Requirements and procedures under Citizenship Act, 1955
UPSC trap: Registration mentioned in Constitution, naturalization only in Act

concepts.name: Undivided India: Territorial Scope
key_dimensions: Includes present-day India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh
Relevance for Article 8 (persons of Indian origin)
Relevance for determining 'born in India' under Article 5
UPSC trap: Burma (Myanmar) was separated in 1937, before partition

concepts.name: Six Months Residence Requirement
key_dimensions: Applicable to migrants from Pakistan after July 19, 1948 (Article 6)
Ordinary residence immediately before registration application
Distinction from five years residence for naturalization
UPSC trap: Different residence periods for different citizenship modes

concepts.name: Permit for Resettlement: Article 7 Exception
key_dimensions: Issued by Government of India for permanent return
Restores citizenship rights lost by migration to Pakistan
Distinction between permit for resettlement and visa for visit
Administrative discretion in granting permits

concepts.name: Constitutional vs Statutory Citizenship Provisions
key_dimensions: Articles 5-11: Constitutional framework at commencement
Citizenship Act, 1955: Detailed statutory provisions
Parliament's power under Article 11 to amend citizenship laws
UPSC trap: Constitutional provisions are basic, Act provides detailed mechanisms

concepts.name: Single Citizenship: Indian Federal Model
key_dimensions: Only Indian citizenship, no separate state citizenship
Contrast with USA (dual citizenship - federal and state)
Implications for freedom of movement and residence (Article 19)
UPSC trap: Despite federal structure, India has unitary citizenship

concepts.name: Citizenship at Commencement vs Subsequent Acquisition
key_dimensions: Articles 5-8: Citizenship at commencement (January 26, 1950)
Articles 9-11: Continuing provisions and regulatory framework
Citizenship Act, 1955: Post-commencement acquisition modes
UPSC trap: Commencement provisions are one-time, not applicable after 1950

concepts.name: Parent/Grandparent Born in India: Criteria
key_dimensions: Relevant for Article 5 (parent born in India) and Article 8 (grandparent)
Undivided India vs Republic of India distinction
Proof requirements and documentation
UPSC trap: Article 5 requires parent, Article 8 allows grandparent

concepts.name: Exclusions and Disqualifications at Commencement
key_dimensions: Persons who migrated to Pakistan after March 1, 1947 (Article 7)
Persons who voluntarily acquired foreign citizenship (Article 9)
No provision for enemy aliens or persons of unsound mind at commencement
UPSC trap: Limited grounds for disqualification in Constitution vs broader in Act

concepts.name: Judicial Interpretation: Citizenship at Commencement Cases
key_dimensions: State of West Bengal vs Anwar Ali Sarkar (1952) - citizenship determination
Izhar Ahmad Khan vs Union of India (1962) - Article 6 interpretation
Distinction between citizenship rights and fundamental rights
UPSC trap: Limited case law on commencement provisions as they were one-time
